title: Adding a very tall horizontal panel can make edit mode barely usable as it covers the popup
line: Panel height can no longer be raised so far that the Panel Settings dialog no longer fits on screen next to the panel.
explanation: The Panel Height spinbox allowed up to half the screen, regardless of the space the Panel Settings dialog needs. On a 1280x800 screen a 400 px top panel left only ~340 px for a ~500 px dialog, so it opened under the panel or ran past the bottom of the screen, hiding the height spinbox and the Delete/Close buttons needed to undo it. The spinbox maximum is now also limited to the panel's current thickness plus the free screen space left after the dialog (and still at most half the screen), and never below the current thickness, so an already thick panel shows its real value and can be shrunk.

commits.message:
panelconfiguration: keep Panel Settings reachable on very thick panels

A panel could be made as thick as half the screen, leaving no room for
the Panel Settings dialog next to it, so the dialog ran off the screen
and could not be used to undo it. Cap the thickness to leave it room.

BUG: 525375

patches.diff:
From f9a2c1158ffc9992132426ae6a250b44d1e0b7f7 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Niccol=C3=B2=20Venerandi?= <niccolo@venerandi.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 04:35:54 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] panelconfiguration: keep Panel Settings reachable on very
 thick panels

A panel could be made as thick as half the screen, leaving no room for
the Panel Settings dialog next to it, so the dialog ran off the screen
and could not be used to undo it. Cap the thickness to leave it room.

BUG: 525375
---
 .../contents/configuration/PanelConfiguration.qml     | 11 ++++++++---
 1 file changed, 8 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-)

diff --git a/desktoppackage/contents/configuration/PanelConfiguration.qml b/desktoppackage/contents/configuration/PanelConfiguration.qml
index cb897a1f04..96140a440c 100644
--- a/desktoppackage/contents/configuration/PanelConfiguration.qml
+++ b/desktoppackage/contents/configuration/PanelConfiguration.qml
@@ -643,9 +643,14 @@ ColumnLayout {
             editable: true
             focus: !Kirigami.InputMethod.willShowOnActive
             from: Math.max(20, panel.minThickness) // below this size, the panel is mostly unusable
-            to: panel.location === PlasmaCore.Types.LeftEdge || panel.location === PlasmaCore.Types.RightEdge
-                ? panel.screenToFollow.geometry.width / 2
-                : panel.screenToFollow.geometry.height / 2
+            to: {
+                const available = plasmoid.availableScreenRect
+                const ownThickness = panel.visibilityMode === Panel.AutoHide ? 0 : panel.thickness
+                const maximum = dialogRoot.vertical
+                    ? Math.min(panel.screenToFollow.geometry.width / 2, available.width + ownThickness - dialogRoot.panelConfiguration.width - dialogRoot.panelConfiguration.margin * 2)
+                    : Math.min(panel.screenToFollow.geometry.height / 2, available.height + ownThickness - dialogRoot.panelConfiguration.height - dialogRoot.panelConfiguration.margin * 2)
+                return Math.max(from, panel.thickness, maximum)
+            }
 
             stepSize: 2
 
-- 
2.53.0

media.caption: Master: top panel set to 400 px, edit mode re-entered: Panel Settings starts under the panel and runs off the bottom of the screen; Panel Height, Delete and Close are unreachable
With the fix: typing 999 caps the height at 218 px (+ disabled); after re-entering edit mode the whole dialog fits between the panels

reviews.text: Capping the panel thickness spinbox to availableScreenRect minus the Panel Settings dialog height is the wrong layer and a bad UX trade-off: on smaller or HiDPI-scaled screens (e.g. 1080p at 175% scaling) the ~500 px dialog leaves almost no room for even normal panels when another panel exists, and it still fails whenever a panel is already thick or a wide vertical panel is moved to a horizontal edge via Set Position. Even within this approach, checking `panel.visibilityMode === Panel.AutoHide` is buggy because `DodgeWindows` and `WindowsGoBelow` also do not reserve space in `availableScreenRect`, causing `to` to double-count `panel.thickness` and ratchet up to half the screen. The real fix belongs in `PanelConfigView` (`plasma-workspace`) so the settings popup stays clamped on-screen and above the panel regardless of panel thickness.
changes: Fix `PanelConfigView` placement and stacking in `plasma-workspace` (`shell/panelconfigview.cpp`) so the Panel Settings window stays fully on-screen and reachable above the panel even for thick panels, rotated vertical panels, or small/scaled screens.

If any thickness cap in `PanelConfiguration.qml` is kept at all, do not tie it to the Panel Settings dialog height in a way that breaks scaled/small screens, and fix the `ownThickness` check to test `panel.visibilityMode === Panel.NormalPanel` (the only mode that reserves space in `availableScreenRect`) while also accounting for the Panel Ruler in `Panel.Custom` width mode.

reviews.text: The diagnosis is right and the evidence shows the dialog fitting at the new 218 px cap, but capping the spinbox treats the symptom at the wrong place: the dialog still runs off screen for any panel that is already thicker than the cap (existing configs, scripts), or that becomes too thick later when the screen resolution or scale drops, another panel is added, or the dialog grows (translations, larger fonts). The notes admit this case is left broken, and the reporter's minimum expectation is that a huge panel can always be undone. It also ties a user-visible limit to the config dialog's height, which costs a lot on small screens (218 px instead of 400 here, ~200 on 1366x768), and it ignores the floating-panel gap.
changes: Make the Panel Settings dialog itself always fit on screen (e.g. in PanelConfigView positioning, let it overlap the panel or clamp it to the available screen area, scrolling its contents if needed), so even panels that are already too thick can be shrunk or deleted.
If a thickness cap is kept as well, keep it as a secondary safeguard and show on the rig that a panel already thicker than the cap (e.g. set to 400 via appletsrc) gets a fully usable dialog.
